# Bun 1.4.0 differential corpus

`registry`, `local`, `link`, and `patch` were generated with the repository's
pinned Bun 1.4.0 (`34cbb9a40`). They cover registry, scoped, alias, workspace, file, link,
root, local and remote tarball, GitHub, optional, peer, platform, override,
catalog, trusted dependency, lifecycle-capable, and native-package resolutions.
The local tarball was produced with `bun pm pack` from `local/vendor/tar-source`.

`private-registry/bun.lock` is a credential-free adaptation of Bun's textual
lockfile output: only the registry URL was replaced with the reserved
`registry.example.test` host. It is not installed by the tests.

`compatibility.lock` records the `folder:` textual resolution accepted by the
parser. Bun 1.4.0 normalizes newly generated directory dependencies to `file:`;
the fixture exists to prevent compatibility with older textual locks regressing.

The patch was created with `bun patch is-number`, a one-line source edit, and
`bun patch --commit node_modules/is-number`. `is-number` is MIT licensed; the
fixture retains only Bun's generated patch and lock metadata, not package source.

Registry package metadata and integrity hashes come from the public npm registry.
The registry lock repairs loong64, mips64el, riscv64, NetBSD, and OpenHarmony
platform identifiers that Bun 1.4.0 serializes as `none` because its platform
enums do not contain them.
The GitHub fixture resolves inspect-js/is-number-object at commit `5181bb2`.
Both GitHub shorthand and `git+https` declarations are present; Bun normalizes
the GitHub HTTPS declaration to the same pinned `github:` lock resolution.
No fixture contains credentials, registry tokens, generated `node_modules`, or a
package-manager cache.

`registry/bun.nix` is generated by this crate. `production-links.txt` is the sorted symlink tree from Bun 1.4.0 using `--frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --linker=isolated --production --filter corpus-registry`; the root flake recreates that tree from the generated cache with networking disabled.

Patch and global-link fixtures prove actionable rejection: patched cache identities are not yet
modeled, and Bun records only the global link name rather than its registered source path.
